tool_input.command:
mkdir -p forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager tests
cat > forgemyspec-board.yaml <<'EOF'
- id: R1
  status: doing
  title: "CLI Task Manager (task_manager.py, sqlite3)"
  quote: "Build a CLI Task Manager in Python. Add, list, update, delete tasks (CRUD)... Persist data in SQLite... Filter by status and priority. Mark task as done. Output as formatted table. Single file CLI: task_manager.py. stdlib only."
  steps:
    - {do: "Spec written and lint passes", check: "cmd: PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager/spec.yaml --formal"}
    - {do: "User approves the spec-only bundle", ok: false}
    - {do: "Implement task_manager.py and boundary tests; gate passes", ok: false}
  next: "spec approval by the user"
EOF
cat > forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager/spec.yaml <<'EOF'
version: "0.1"
title: "CLI Task Manager"
objective: "A single-file Python CLI (task_manager.py) that manages tasks with CRUD, filtering and done-marking, persisted in SQLite via raw sqlite3 and printed as a terminal table."
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Empty Python repository, stdlib only (argparse, sqlite3, unittest). Entry point task_manager.py at the repository root; tests in tests/."
  assumptions:
    - "Database path defaults to tasks.db in the current directory and can be overridden with --db or the TASK_DB environment variable."
    - "due_date is optional and is an ISO date YYYY-MM-DD; description is optional (empty by default)."
    - "Default priority is medium and default status is todo on add."
    - "id is an auto-incrementing integer assigned by SQLite."
    - "Filters combine with AND; list is ordered by id."
    - "Invalid input or unknown id prints an error to stderr and exits with code 1 (argparse usage errors exit 2)."
constraints:
  - "No ORM and no third-party packages; only the Python standard library."
  - "All code lives in the single file task_manager.py; tests are separate."
  - "SQL uses parameterized queries, never string-formatted values."
  - "No web UI, no authentication, no sync, no recurring tasks, no tags or subtasks."
success_criteria:
  - "add, list, update, delete and done commands work end to end against a real SQLite file."
  - "list --status and --priority return only matching tasks."
  - "list prints an aligned table with a header row."
  - "Tasks survive across separate invocations."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "add creates a task with id, title, description, priority, status and due_date and persists it in SQLite.", confidence: 0.95}
  - {id: h2, description: "list shows all tasks and filters by status and by priority, combined with AND.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h3, description: "update changes only the given fields of an existing task and delete removes it; an unknown id is reported as an error.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h4, description: "done sets the status of a task to done.", confidence: 0.95}
  - {id: h5, description: "Invalid priority, status, title or due_date is rejected with an error and exit code 1, and nothing is stored.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h6, description: "list output is a formatted table with a header row and aligned columns.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h7, description: "Data persists in a SQLite file using raw sqlite3, with only stdlib dependencies, in the single file task_manager.py.", confidence: 0.9}
required_evidence:
  - "Output of python3 -m unittest discover tests showing all boundary tests passing."
  - "Output of the gate command ending in RESULT: PASS."
  - "Sample CLI session output showing add, list with filters, update, done and delete."
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Design the schema, CLI subcommands and validation rules.", type: design, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h5, h7]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Implement the database layer and commands in task_manager.py.", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h7]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Implement validation and the table formatter.", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h5, h6]}
  - {id: a4, description: "Write and run the unittest boundary tests and the gate.", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7]}
decision_rules:
  - "If a requirement is ambiguous (for example due_date format), stop and ask the user before changing the spec."
  - "Anything outside the obligations is a spec amendment, not an implementation choice."
  - "Stop if a gate stage fails and fix the cause; never weaken tests."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a CLI Task Manager in Python. Requirements: Add, list, update, delete tasks (CRUD). Each task has: id, title, description, priority (low/medium/high), status (todo/in-progress/done), due_date. Persist data in SQLite (no ORM, raw sqlite3). Filter tasks by status and priority. Mark task as done. Output as formatted table in terminal. Single file CLI entry point: task_manager.py. No external dependencies beyond stdlib."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "add, list, update, delete tasks"
      - "priority low/medium/high"
      - "status todo/in-progress/done"
      - "persist in SQLite with raw sqlite3"
      - "filter by status and priority"
      - "mark task as done"
      - "formatted table output"
      - "single file task_manager.py"
      - "stdlib only"
formal:
  module: TaskManager
  obligations:
    - id: crud_roundtrip
      kind: boundary
      statement: "add stores a task with id, title, description, priority, status and due_date; update changes only given fields; delete removes it; unknown id exits 1."
      hypotheses: [h1, h3]
      must_include: ["add, list, update, delete tasks"]
      test: "test_task_manager.CrudTests.test_add_update_delete_roundtrip"
    - id: enum_validation
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Priority outside low/medium/high, status outside todo/in-progress/done, empty title or malformed due_date exits 1 and stores nothing."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["priority low/medium/high", "status todo/in-progress/done"]
      test: "test_task_manager.ValidationTests.test_invalid_values_rejected"
    - id: sqlite_persistence
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Tasks written by one process invocation are read by the next from the SQLite file, using raw sqlite3 with parameterized queries."
      hypotheses: [h1, h7]
      must_include: ["persist in SQLite with raw sqlite3"]
      test: "test_task_manager.PersistenceTests.test_persists_across_invocations"
    - id: filter_status_priority
      kind: boundary
      statement: "list --status and --priority return only matching tasks, and both together apply AND."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["filter by status and priority"]
      test: "test_task_manager.FilterTests.test_filter_by_status_and_priority"
    - id: mark_done
      kind: boundary
      statement: "done <id> sets status to done and leaves other fields unchanged; unknown id exits 1."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["mark task as done"]
      test: "test_task_manager.DoneTests.test_done_sets_status"
    - id: table_output
      kind: boundary
      statement: "list prints a header row (ID, TITLE, PRIORITY, STATUS, DUE) and aligned columns, one row per task."
      hypotheses: [h6]
      must_include: ["formatted table output"]
      test: "test_task_manager.TableTests.test_table_has_header_and_aligned_columns"
    - id: single_file_stdlib
      kind: boundary
      statement: "task_manager.py imports only stdlib modules and runs standalone as the CLI entry point."
      hypotheses: [h7]
      must_include: ["single file task_manager.py", "stdlib only"]
      test: "test_task_manager.StructureTests.test_stdlib_only_single_file"
scope:
  paths: ["task_manager.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
EOF
H="PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness python3 -m forgemyspec"
eval $H lint forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager/spec.yaml --formal && eval $H package forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager/spec.yaml

I couldn't put the request on the board. Both guard hooks refused to write `forgemyspec-board.yaml`, because no approved spec covers that path. Once you approve the spec, I'll add it. You can also add the path to `allow_paths` in `.forgemyspec/config.yaml` if you want it writable sooner.

**What the spec covers** (`forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager/spec.yaml`). All seven obligations are checked by Python tests, with no Dafny proof, since nothing here is critical logic:

| id | statement |
|---|---|
| `crud_roundtrip` | add, update and delete work; an unknown id exits 1 |
| `enum_validation` | a bad priority, status, title or due date exits 1 and stores nothing |
| `sqlite_persistence` | tasks survive across separate invocations, using raw sqlite3 with parameterized queries |
| `filter_status_priority` | `--status` and `--priority` filter the list, and both together apply AND |
| `mark_done` | `done <id>` sets the status to done and leaves the other fields alone |
| `table_output` | the table has a header row and aligned columns |
| `single_file_stdlib` | `task_manager.py` is a single file that imports only the standard library |

**Assumptions I made.** Tell me if any are wrong:
- The database defaults to `tasks.db` in the current directory. `--db` or the `TASK_DB` environment variable overrides it.
- `due_date` is an optional date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, and the description is optional.
- A new task defaults to priority medium and status todo.
- Errors go to stderr and exit with code 1. Usage errors from argparse exit with code 2.

**To approve:** type the code `CUJFFJ` in this chat. It approves `forgemyspec-bundle/task-manager` (content `c3b182b85128`). After that I'll run `approve`, implement `task_manager.py` with its tests, and run the gate until it passes.
